result_text:
I implemented all five requirements in `src/battery/bms.py` and added tests in `tests/test_bms.py`, but I haven't run them. Bash was denied in this session, so `python3 -m pytest` still needs a run on your side.

- **Code:** `cell_fault` faults above 4.20 V or below 3.00 V, with both limits themselves allowed (BMS-001, BMS-002). `charge_permitted` allows 0 to 45 °C inclusive (BMS-003). `BatteryController.step` goes to FAULT on a cell fault and stays there once latched. Otherwise it is CHARGING when the charger is connected and charging is permitted, and IDLE if not (BMS-004, BMS-005). `reset` returns FAULT to IDLE only when the cells passed in are healthy, and does nothing in other states (BMS-005).
- **Convention:** I put `# implements:` markers above each function, the class and its methods, as CONTRIBUTING.md asks. I added no helpers.
- **Tests:** The 13 tests carry `@pytest.mark.verifies(...)` and cover each acceptance criterion, including both sides of every boundary. I also added tests that:
  - one bad cell among several triggers a fault;
  - charging returns to IDLE when the charger is disconnected;
  - `reset` is a no-op when the controller isn't faulted.
- **Ambiguity:** BMS-004 and BMS-005 don't say what happens to `reset` outside FAULT or to an empty cell list. I made `reset` a no-op outside FAULT and treated an empty list as no fault. I didn't record these in `FINDINGS.json`.
